items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: So I called him and I said, “Are you going to bring your accordion?” He goes, “Well.” I said, “Well bring it, maybe we’ll do a duet.” And then before the gig he introduced me to Al. I said, “Well Al would you come and join us?”

ctx.x: Do you think you play differently when the length of your improvisation is open ended? Like last night you pretty much can decide as you’re playing how many choruses you’re going to do, where if you’re playing a solo with a band that — you’re not leading it, perhaps you know I need to limit myself. So is there a thought process that you take that into account? Like I’m going to do two choruses so do you play differently if you have a time limit?

Yes. I mean well for instance last night it was more open-ended and I didn’t have to limit, as you said, limit myself. I could do one, two, three or four or five. Like there was a period where that accordion player, Al, came up and sat in right. So now we’re incorporating a guy who does polka music with the accordion, because Ron Oswanski also is an amazing accordion player and can do the polkas, he grew up in a Polish household and he played all that stuff. But he also can improvise and play jazz, he’s…

figure out what — so then we did this Ukrainian polka because of the Ukrainian situation. But Ron and I had done, I had to produce an album for Ron and we did that song on his record but we did it kind of like as a North African kind of vibe combined with this polka. So we tried to do that last night with Al but then on that I didn’t really improvise. I kind of let Al — which I played the melody with him and then just a little tiny solo, Ron would play a little solo, so just it was more about how do we feature,…
